overview.title: Shared style, separate positions
overview.explanation: Each hollow-diamond link is explicitly labeled shared owner, rather than exclusive composition. Both marks reach the same immutable Style but keep separate x members. The pool keeps another strong owner. A reference count tracks these owners; the Style is destroyed only after the last strong owner releases it. The diagram uses shared aggregation to show the non-exclusive relationship; the C++ shared_ptr contract supplies the precise lifetime rule.

focus.title: Reuse by the complete intrinsic key
focus.start: // The key covers all shared fields.
focus.what: The pool asks whether an exactly matching style already exists.
focus.where: This branch occurs after input validation and before allocation.
focus.why: A structured complete key prevents accidental sharing of different styles.
focus.invariant: Equal keys mean interchangeable immutable style data.
focus.risk: Omitting size or another intrinsic field returns the wrong shared object.

focus.title: Combine shared style with local position
focus.what: A mark formats shared style information together with its own position.
focus.where: This read-only operation is the visible use of the flyweight.
focus.why: The same Style supports many distinct Mark contexts.
focus.invariant: Position stays local and the Style remains immutable.
focus.risk: Returning a borrowed local string or mutating shared style would break isolation.
explain: Declare a read-only operation that returns an owned string.
The comment identifies position as per-use state.
Borrow the shared name for this call.
Copy the small shared size value.
Begin the result with the style name and separator.
Append the size converted to decimal text.
Append this Mark position to the result.
Close drawing; the returned string survives its locals.
